name: Exploring without computing gradients
gist: Some optimization problems don't allow gradient calculation (black-box functions, limited queries). How do algorithms work with only function values, simulations, or search?
explain: Gradients are not always available. Imagine optimizing a design where you can only build a prototype, test it in the wind tunnel, and measure its performance—you get one number (drag coefficient) but no gradient. Or you are tuning hyperparameters of a large model—trying different learning rates, layer sizes, regularization strengths—and each experiment takes hours to run. You cannot compute gradients; you can only try different settings and see if they work better or worse. These are black-box optimization problems, where you interact with the system by querying it but never see its internals.

The challenge is that you have a limited budget of queries. You might afford 100 experiments before your budget runs out, and there could be millions of settings to explore. Randomly sampling does not work—you would waste most of your budget on obviously bad settings. You need a strategy that uses early results to focus the search on promising regions without wasting queries on dead ends. Traditional methods like genetic algorithms can work but are slow. The question is: how do you learn a model of how changes affect the outcome, and use that model to guide your next query?

Papers in this space use several approaches. Bayesian optimization maintains a probabilistic belief about what settings are good, then uses that belief to decide which settings to try next, balancing exploration (trying new areas) and exploitation (refining known good areas). Some papers use gradient-free neural networks that learn from function values directly. Others treat it as a search problem: divide the space into regions and eliminate regions that look bad based on samples from them. A few use evolutionary strategies where you maintain a population of settings, measure them all, and breed new ones from the best. Simulation-based optimization treats the black box as a simulator and uses the results from many cheap simulations to guide expensive real experiments. The insight is that you do not need gradients to learn how responses change; function values alone are enough if you model the patterns across the space.

papers.title: Contextual Causal Bayesian Optimisation
papers.contribution: Derives worst-case and instance-dependent high-probability regret bounds, achieving sublinear regret with reduced sample complexity in high-dimensional settings.

papers.title: Graph Random Features for Scalable Gaussian Processes
papers.contribution: Enables Bayesian optimization on over 1M graph nodes on a single computer with wall-clock speedups and memory savings while preserving competitive performance.

papers.title: Incorporating Expert Priors into Bayesian Optimization via Dynamic Mean Decay
papers.contribution: Accelerates convergence with informative priors and remains robust against biased ones, with convergence guarantees and compatibility across acquisition functions.

papers.title: Many Needles in a Haystack: Active Hit Discovery for Perturbation Experiments
papers.contribution: The approach achieves asymptotic optimality with empirical improvements up to 6.4% on real immunology datasets including the Schmidt IL-2 dataset.

papers.title: RefineEvo: Planning-Guided Heuristic Evolution with Bidirectional Experience
papers.contribution: RefineEvo outperforms strong baselines on classic combinatorial optimization benchmarks with superior solution quality while improving token efficiency.

papers.title: Romberg-Extrapolated Zeroth-Order Gradient Estimator: Higher-Order Bias Reduction with Preserved Leading Directional Variance
papers.contribution: Demonstrates faster and more stable zeroth-order SGD on synthetic benchmarks, simulator-based wireless optimization, and black-box prompt tuning.

papers.title: Symmetry-Aware Bayesian Optimization via Max Kernels
papers.contribution: The projected max kernel achieves significantly lower regret on synthetic and real-world BO benchmarks without increasing computational complexity compared to existing invariant and non-invariant kernels.

papers.title: Turning Stale Gradients into Stable Gradients: Coherent Coordinate Descent with Implicit Landscape Smoothing for Lightweight Zeroth-Order Op
papers.contribution: Demonstrates CoCD significantly outperforms Block Cyclic Coordinate Descent and randomized ZO methods on MLP, CNN, and ResNet architectures up to 270k parameters.

papers.title: A Language-Guided Bayesian Optimization for Efficient LoRA Hyperparameter Search
papers.contribution: Discovers hyperparameters achieving 20% performance improvement over standard choices using only about 30 iterations versus 45,000 combinations.

papers.title: ALAS: Additive Learnable Alpha-Stable Kernels for Flexible Bayesian Optimization
papers.contribution: Demonstrate strong and robust performance on standard benchmarks and real-world surrogates across diverse settings.

papers.title: Adaptive Acquisition Selection for Bayesian Optimization with Large Language Models
papers.contribution: LMABO demonstrates significant performance improvement over strong baselines across 50 benchmark problems by adaptively selecting acquisition functions based on complete optimization state.

papers.title: Bridging Spherical Black-Box Optimizers
papers.contribution: Hybrid optimizers (ES-OVI and CBO-OVI) enable control over flat-minima preference and achieve competitive results on language model merging and locomotion tasks with limited budgets.

papers.title: Combinatorial Bandit Bayesian Optimization for Tensor Outputs
papers.contribution: Tensor-output BO methods achieve sublinear regret bounds; on real-world experiments, CBBO demonstrates superiority by handling partially observed tensor outputs and optimizing over output subsets.

papers.title: Cost-aware Stopping for Bayesian Optimization
papers.contribution: The policy provides finite-sample guarantees bounding cost-adjusted simple regret and usually matches or outperforms other acquisition-stopping pairs.

papers.title: Efficient Sliced Wasserstein Distance Computation via Adaptive Bayesian Optimization
papers.contribution: The BO-based direction selection achieves state-of-the-art performance and comparable convergence to QSW variants with modest overhead, enabling efficient SW computation in optimization loops.

papers.title: From Sorting Algorithms to Scalable Kernels: Bayesian Optimization in High-Dimensional Permutation Spaces
papers.contribution: Merge Kernel outperforms Mallows kernel in both optimization performance and computational efficiency as dimension grows, enabling previously intractable problems.

papers.title: GIT-BO: High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization with Tabular Foundation Models
papers.contribution: GIT-BO delivers stronger performance-time trade-offs than state-of-the-art GP-based methods across 60 problem variants up to 500 dimensions, with runtime advantages growing with dimensionality.

papers.title: Iterated Population Based Training with Task-Agnostic Restarts
papers.contribution: Matches or outperforms 5 prior PBT variants and other HPO algorithms on average across 8 tasks without requiring budget increases or hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: LILO: Bayesian Optimization with Natural Language Feedback
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms conventional preference-based BO and LLM-only optimizers, with particularly strong gains in feedback-limited regimes.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Evolutionary Program Synthesis for Quasi-Monte Carlo Design
papers.contribution: The method discovers new best-known 2D point sets for N≥40, improves 3D benchmarks beyond proven frontiers, and finds better Sobol parameters for option-pricing tasks.

papers.title: LLM4Branch: Large Language Model for Discovering Efficient Branching Policies of Integer Programs
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among CPU-based methods and competitive performance with GPU-based models on standard MILP benchmarks.

papers.title: Learning Dynamics of Zeroth-Order Optimization: A Kernel Perspective
papers.contribution: Shows approximation error depends on model output size rather than parameter dimension, explaining ZO scalability to LLMs.

papers.title: Local Entropy Search over Descent Sequences for Bayesian Optimization
papers.contribution: LES achieves strong sample efficiency compared to existing local and global Bayesian optimization methods on high-complexity synthetic objectives and benchmark problems.

papers.title: Meta-Black-Box Optimization Can Do Search Guidance for Expensive Constrained Multi-Objective Optimization
papers.contribution: Outperforms baselines across diverse benchmarks and generalizes across varying problem dimensions, population sizes, and numbers of objectives.

papers.title: Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization via Adaptive $\varepsilon$-Constraint Decomposition
papers.contribution: Provides uniform Pareto coverage without hypervolume computation, handles constraints and preferences naturally, and demonstrates superior coverage and competitive hypervolume performance against state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: On Regret Bounds of Thompson Sampling for Bayesian Optimization
papers.contribution: Show GP-TS suffers polynomial dependence on 1/δ with probability δ; provide improved regret bounds on time horizon T matching theoretical structure.

papers.title: Online Black-Box Prompt Optimization with Regret Guarantees under Noisy Feedback
papers.contribution: Achieves sublinear regret convergence and outperforms existing black-box methods with better stability in online scenarios.

papers.title: Probability of Matching for Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
papers.contribution: POM-guided batch MOBO consistently outperforms baselines on standard MOBO metrics and a new design-space coverage metric (Expected Minimum Distance).

papers.title: Regime-Adaptive Bayesian Optimization via Dirichlet Process Mixtures of Gaussian Processes
papers.contribution: Consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on molecular conformer optimization, virtual screening, and fusion reactor design across multi-regime objectives.

papers.title: Taking the GP Out of the Loop
papers.contribution: TuRBO-ENN reduces proposal time by one to two orders of magnitude compared to TuRBO at up to 50,000 observations without sacrificing solution quality.

papers.title: Tractable Expected Information Gains for Exponential Family Posteriors
papers.contribution: Achieves superior convergence rates and substantial performance gains for sequential design compared to standard nested estimators.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Optimization at the Edge of Stability
papers.contribution: Finds ZO methods operate at the edge of stability with implicit regularization specific to ZO where large step sizes regularize Hessian trace rather than top eigenvalue.
